Straight Talk

Buyer & Seller Tips

A few things worth knowing before you buy, sell, or spend money on a renovation.

This comes from working both sides of real estate — as an agent, and as someone who's actually built property from the ground up. Take what's useful.

For Buyers For Sellers Renovation ROI

For Buyers

Things worth knowing before you buy

01Get pre-approved before you fall in love

Not pre-qualified. Pre-approved. Know your real number before you start touring houses you can't actually get financed on.

02Don't skip the inspection to win a bid

I get why people do it in a hot market. I still think it's a bad idea. An inspection is the cheapest insurance you'll ever buy on the biggest purchase of your life.

03Budget for what the house needs, not just what it costs

The purchase price is step one. Roof age, furnace age, foundation condition — that's the real number. I'll walk it with you and tell you what I'm actually seeing.

04Location problems can't be renovated away

You can fix a kitchen. You can't fix being on a busy road, or backing up to a commercial lot. Know what you can change and what you're stuck with.

05The lowest price isn't always the best deal

Cheap houses are sometimes cheap for a reason. I'll tell you when that reason is a good one to walk away from.

06Ask what's permitted and what isn't

That finished basement or converted garage might not be permitted work. That matters for insurance, resale, and whether it's actually safe.

For Sellers

Things worth knowing before you sell

01Price it right the first time

Overpricing and sitting on the market for 60 days does more damage than starting slightly conservative. Buyers notice a stale listing.

02Not every upgrade pays you back

I've built houses. I know what things actually cost versus what they actually return. I'll tell you which projects are worth it before you spend the money — see the ROI breakdown below.

03Curb appeal sells the showing, not just the house

Buyers decide how they feel about a house before they're through the front door. A weekend of cleanup outside is the cheapest ROI you'll find.

04Disclose everything

It protects you more than it hurts you. Problems that come out during inspection instead of upfront cost you trust and, usually, more money.

05Timing the market is a gamble. Timing your life isn't.

Nobody can tell you exactly where rates or prices go next. I can help you figure out if now is right for your situation, which is the only timing that actually matters.

06A clean inspection is worth more than a bidding war

A house that shows well and inspects clean will out-perform a house that wins on price but scares off buyers at inspection. Fix the real issues before you list.

From Someone Who's Actually Built Them

Renovation ROI, straight up

Here's my honest read on the upgrades people ask about most before selling — based on years of building and knowing what things actually cost, not just guessing.

Project
Verdict
Why
Full kitchen remodel
Usually skip it
A $50,000 kitchen rarely brings back $50,000 at closing. If it's not falling apart, a smaller refresh usually makes more sense.
Fresh paint, inside & out
Do it
One of the highest-return, lowest-cost things you can do before listing. Almost always worth it.
New roof
Depends
If it's near the end of its life, buyers and inspectors will flag it regardless. Sometimes worth doing, sometimes worth pricing in instead.
Bathroom refresh
Depends
A dated but functional bathroom is rarely worth a full gut. Fixtures, grout, and a good clean often get you most of the benefit.
Landscaping / curb appeal
Do it
Cheap, fast, and it's the first thing every buyer sees. Consistently one of the better returns out there.
Finishing a basement
Usually skip it
Expensive, and appraisers often don't value it the way you'd hope. Fine if you're staying long-term — not a great pre-sale move.

The Bottom Line

Every property's different. This is where a conversation beats a checklist.
